discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition. This result established atomic gases as programmable quantum simulators of strongly correlated matter, in the spirit of Feynman's proposal. Greiner and Bloch then developed quantum gas microscopes, which image and control individual atoms in lattices. With them they observed antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, entanglement entropy and many-body localization. Zoller's theory, including lattice gauge theories, topological phases and Rydberg dressing, gave the field its roadmap. Laboratories worldwide now use this platform, and it bridges condensed-matter physics and quantum information science. It is the direct ancestor of today's programmable neutral-atom quantum processors. Together these contributions opened a new way to explore quantum many-body physics from the bottom up.
